implementation_notes: Pekko Streams provides the enrichment stage directly: mapAsync(parallelism)(msg => lookup(msg.key)) passes each element to a Future-returning function, keeps at most n lookups in flight and preserves order, while Reactive Streams backpressure stops the source from outrunning the resource (it backpressures once n futures are pending). Failures fail the stream unless a supervision strategy or recover is attached, so the degraded path is explicit; mapAsyncUnordered is the variant when ordering does not matter. The resource client is an injected class, which keeps the stage testable.
code_sketch:
def lookup(id: String): Future[Customer] = customerClient.find(id)   // resource call

orders
  .mapAsync(8)(o => lookup(o.customerId).map(c => o.copy(customerName = Some(c.name))))
  .recover { case _: SourceError => Order.unenriched }   // explicit degraded path
  .runWith(Sink.foreach(_.toString))
pitfalls: mapAsync emits in input order, so one slow lookup stalls the stage even with free parallelism; use mapAsyncUnordered when order is irrelevant.
A failed Future fails the whole stream - attach recover/recoverWith or a supervision strategy if enrichment is optional.
parallelism is per stage, not per resource: raising it without bounding the client's connection pool just moves the queue into the resource.

variants.name: cats-effect IO enrichment with parTraverse
variants.implementation_notes: In an effect-typed codebase the enricher is a function returning IO: it reads the key, calls the resource through a client, merges, and the runtime supplies async, cancellation and the error channel - nothing blocks a thread. Independent lookups for a batch run with parTraverse/parSequence under the Parallel[IO] instance, and the effect can be memoized per key behind an explicit cache; 'resource unavailable' stays in the error type, so callers must choose between failing and degrading. Choose it when the service is already written against cats-effect or ZIO.
pitfalls: parTraverse starts one effect per element with no bound, so a large batch becomes an unbounded fan-out - chunk it or gate it with a Semaphore.
IO is a description, not a value: memoizing by key needs an explicit cache (Ref/ConcurrentHashMap), otherwise every run re-executes the effect.
handleErrorWith into a default hides a broken resource; make the degradation visible (log, metric, or tag the message as unenriched).
